Islam is built on five: testifying that none is worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger, prayer, zakat, Hajj and fasting in Ramadan.
A man from Najd asked about Islam, was told five prayers, the Ramadan fast and zakat, with more only if he wished, and swore to do no more nor less.
Gabriel came as a man and asked the Prophet about faith, Islam, excellence and the Hour, and the Prophet named its signs and said only Allah knows its time.
The Prophet told the Abdul Qais delegation that belief in Allah alone means the testimony, prayer, zakat, the Ramadan fast and a fifth of booty, and forbade four wine vessels.
Dimam bin Tha'laba adjured the Prophet by Allah to confirm his mission to all mankind, five prayers, the Ramadan fast and zakat, then declared his belief as his people's envoy.
The Prophet taught the Abdul Qais delegation the testimony, prayer, zakat, the Ramadan fast and a fifth of booty, forbade four wine vessels, and told them to pass it on.
Whoever says none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, prays like the Muslims, faces their Qibla and eats their slaughter is a Muslim, his blood and property protected.
The Abdul Qais delegation were ordered to believe in Allah, pray, give zakat and pay a fifth of spoils, and forbidden four vessels; Jarir pledged prayer, zakat and good advice.
A man asking about Islam is told of the five daily prayers, Ramadan's fast and zakat, more being voluntary, and will succeed if true to his word.
The Abdul Qais delegation are told to believe in Allah, pray, pay zakat, fast Ramadan and pay a fifth of booty, and are forbidden four vessels used for alcoholic drinks.
A man asks the Prophet what faith, Islam and Ihsan are and when the Hour comes, hears its portents, and the Prophet says it was Gabriel teaching people their religion.
Welcoming the Abdul Qais delegation, the Prophet ordered them to pray, pay Zakat, fast Ramadan and give a fifth of booty, and forbade four kinds of drinking vessels.
